evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: What do you think is the end game path for this company? I mean, given that you sort of are at that intersection of tech where I think the path forward is known and bio, sort of biotech, where the paths a little different. Like what do you can you help me envision what the end state might look like?

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: Can you tell, are there any restrictions or prohibitions or challenges with marketing this project, this product digitally?

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: See I’m torn on this one. We’ve had a strict sort of no tobacco, no cannabis policy at Precursor since I started the fund. And I think for the most part I’ve been happy to have sat both of those markets out. This is the first thing I’ve seen where I think it’s not a wink wink cessation product, but like actually interested in addressing the problem.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: So I’ve never had to sit down and think about under what circumstances would we say yes to a product that I think could actually address… And I have a ton of smokers in my family. So it’s a very personally relevant problem. For now, for now I’m going to pass. But I want to follow up with you and see if I could come up with... Because I’d have to explain sort of to my investors why we’ve decided to change our rules and stance on both of those categories.

rationales.explanation: Charles asks about the company’s end-game path and possible end state, without expressing a positive or negative judgment.
Charles asks whether digital marketing restrictions or prohibitions could affect the product.
Charles expresses astonishment about the biotech path being discussed, but does not state a directional investment judgment.
Charles states that Precursor has maintained a strict no-tobacco, no-cannabis policy and has generally been comfortable excluding those markets.
Charles positively distinguishes this product from superficial cessation positioning and says it is genuinely interested in addressing the problem.
Charles says the smoking problem is personally relevant because he has many smokers in his family.
Charles directly ties his decision to the need to explain to his investors why the fund would change its rules and stance on tobacco and cannabis.

annotation_summary: Charles’s explicit pass is attributed to Precursor’s existing tobacco and cannabis investment-thesis rules and the difficulty of justifying a policy change to investors. His positive view of the product and personal relevance of smoking cessation are recorded as secondary, non-decisive observations.
